rv.q: Pity that the high gloss of director Margot Bordelon's production, amplified by Emilio Sosa's costumes and Jiyoun Chang's lighting, can't cover over this dramedy's shortcomings.

The script by playwright Mansa Ra struggles to find a consistent rhythm that feels like actual people talking to each other. Margot Bordelon's direction doesn't help much; it all adds up to a stagy experience. Too bad, since the concept is a good one.
